data.title: Authentication
data.tagline: Verify who is making the request
data.description: Authentication proves an identity through a password, passkey, one-time code, or trusted provider and then maintains a session. Store credentials safely, limit repeated attempts, and protect recovery paths. After identity is known, Authorization still decides what that person may do.

use: Recover account access through a controlled process
avoid: Treat a user ID sent by the browser as proof of identity
Use long-lived tokens with no revocation plan
Reveal whether a private account exists through detailed errors

lessonPractice.title: A request with a valid session opens My Orders. What must the system establish first?

options.label: Which signed-in user this request belongs to
options.feedback: Correct. Authentication answers who the requester is before the system can decide what they may see.

options.label: That the page displays a user avatar
options.feedback: An avatar is browser display, not server-verifiable identity.

options.label: Whether the user is an admin or a member
options.feedback: A role is an authorization decision made after identity is established.

data.agentPrompt: The orders page currently trusts a userId sent by the browser. Change it to obtain the current user from verified sign-in state before querying orders. Test signed-in and signed-out access: the first must show only that user’s orders, and the second must require sign-in.
